input.question: how do zits form, and why does popping certain zits hurt like a bitch (lip line) and others don't (forehead)
input.ground_truth: There are different kinds of breakout. Whiteheads and blackheads are simply clogged pores; the oil in the pore is either blocked, trapping the bacteria in the pore, or it is exposed to air, where the bacteria oxidizes and forms a whitehead. A pimple, or zit, when the bacteria deeper down in the pore becomes infected and inflamed, and these can be painful. Depending on the location, you can experiences different degrees of pain. There are many more sensitive nerve endings around the lip area, so you feel so many more sensations. That's why kissing someone feels so good, and why cold sores hurt like a mutha.

response.prediction:
Okay, let me explain this in a simple way, like I'm talking to a 5-year-old:

Zits (or pimples) happen when your skin gets clogged with oil and dead skin. Sometimes, germs get stuck in there too, and it causes a little bump or pimple. 

Now, why does it hurt more when you pop certain zits, like the ones near your lips, and not others, like on your forehead? Well, it’s because some parts of your face have more sensitive skin. The skin around your lips is thinner and has more nerves, so when you pop a zit there, it feels more painful. It’s like poking a sore spot on your finger instead of your arm. The skin on your forehead is thicker and less sensitive, so it doesn’t hurt as much when you pop a zit there.

But remember, popping zits isn’t a good idea because it can make your skin hurt more or even leave scars! So, it’s better to let them heal on their own or ask a grown-up for help.
